title: Neurosurgery Resident & GPT-5.6 Sol Prove Crouzeix’s Conjecture in Matrix Analysis
whyItMatters: A Beijing neurosurgery resident with no math PhD used GPT-5.6 Sol to prove Michel Crouzeix’s 22-year-old matrix-analysis conjecture—confirmed by Crouzeix, Greenbaum, and Townsend.
summary: On July 27, 2026, Beijing neurosurgery resident Shanmu Jin posted a preprint proving Crouzeix’s 2004 conjecture (that the numerical range of any matrix is a 2-spectral set), developed via a 16-hour run with GPT-5.6 Sol. Matrix-analysis specialists Michel Crouzeix, Anne Greenbaum, and Alex Townsend independently verified the proof, and a week later Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger published a second independent proof also developed with GPT-5.6 Sol.
technicalHighlights: Settled Crouzeix’s 2004 conjecture on the sharp constant C = 2 bounding ‖p(A)‖ over the numerical range W(A).
Reviewed and endorsed by Michel Crouzeix, Anne Greenbaum, and Alex Townsend (featured in SIAM News).
Landmark demonstration of democratization: a non-specialist physician cracked an active research conjecture using consumer-accessible frontier AI.
caveats: Posted initially as an unrefereed preprint without Lean formalization; formal journal publication is pending despite strong expert consensus and an independent second proof.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolved the central 22-year-old open conjecture in spectral-set theory and numerical linear algebra.
scoreRationale.ripple: Highlighted a major structural shift: domain outsiders can now resolve active math conjectures with frontier AI.
scoreRationale.verification: Checked and confirmed by Crouzeix, Greenbaum, and Townsend, plus an independent second proof days later.
scoreRationale.velocity: Produced in a 16-hour AI run by a medical resident outside academic mathematics.
